questions.heading: Fixed Intervals Block Weeks the Crew Cannot Work
questions.stem: A planner books a crew for a safety course in weeks 5, 6 and 7. Which fixed interval, added to the crew's NoOverlap list, keeps all three weeks free of jobs and no others?

options.says: Size 7 - 5 = 2 is the span [5, 7): it blocks weeks 5 and 6 and lets a job run in week 7. A period given by its first and last week has size last - first + 1.
The second argument is the size, not the last week: this blocks [5, 12), weeks 5 to 11.
The first argument is the start: this blocks weeks 7, 8 and 9 and leaves weeks 5 and 6 open.

questions.heading: The Job Shop Is One NoOverlap per Machine and One Precedence Row per Step
questions.stem: A shop has 4 jobs and 3 machines; every job has 3 steps, one on each machine, in its own order. How many NoOverlap constraints and precedence rows does the job shop model have?

options.says: NoOverlap is per machine, not per job, and precedence links consecutive steps: a 3-step job has 2 rows, not 3.
A NoOverlap per step has one interval in it and constrains nothing; the rule is one NoOverlap per machine.
Right: one NoOverlap per machine, and each job's 3 steps give 2 order rows, 4 x 2 = 8.
A row links step k to step k + 1; a job's first step has no step before it, so each job gives 2 rows.

questions.heading: Optional Intervals Let a Job Choose Its Crew
questions.stem: A modeler gives each job one ordinary interval and puts it in both crews' NoOverlap lists, hoping the solver will pick a crew for each job. What does the solve return?

options.text: A schedule in which each job occupies both crews at once
options.says: Right: an ordinary interval is present in every list it is in, so the job blocks both crews; the lesson's version ends at week 19, against 10 with optional intervals.

options.text: A schedule in which each job occupies just one of the crews
options.says: Nothing in the model lets a job leave a list; choosing a crew needs one optional interval per crew with a presence literal.

options.text: The status INFEASIBLE, as an interval can sit in one list at most
options.says: An interval may appear in several constraints; the lesson's shared-interval model solves to OPTIMAL.

options.text: The status MODEL_INVALID, as the two lists share their intervals
options.says: CP-SAT accepts the model; the lesson's run returns OPTIMAL with a makespan of 19 weeks.
